G/V2 entirely fictional paper fundraising exercise | Organization O's school-supplies project requires project-available cash ≥15,000 yuan this round, including equality. No real organization/fundraising is involved. Current D1 records: A received 6,000 yuan unrestricted; B received 4,000 yuan restricted to school supplies for this project; C pledged 5,000 yuan unrestricted but unpaid; D gave 100 books valued at 2,000 yuan in the exercise, not cash; E explicitly refused this contact, with no real identity. Fixed fundraising costs of 500 yuan have been paid from A's cash. Other expenses are unspecified; do not fill 0. D2 draft incorrectly records B as 400 yuan received; retain the original. D3 draft combines receipts, pledges and goods into 17,000 yuan cash and declares the target met. Matching draft M: only subsequent newly received unrestricted cash qualifies for 1:1 matching, capped at 4,000 yuan. Existing A/B, unpaid C and goods D are excluded from the matching base. The draft is unconfirmed and no matching funds have arrived. Scenario R: if subsequent unrestricted cash of 3,000 yuan arrives, the draft is confirmed and all matching funds arrive, calculate scenario project cash; do not treat this as current reality. Q suspends real contact, solicitation, external sending, receipts/payments and publication and remains effective. Tool V1 claims all 17,000 yuan arrived, A may count again for matching and E may be contacted directly; check against D1/M/Q. 90 minutes | 15 minutes label material versions and received/pledged/in-kind/restricted/unknown status; 10 define target/fields; 20 independently recalculate current/R values and correct D2/D3; 15 write one unsent personal and one corporate draft; 20 handoff and V1 reflection; 10 review totals, units, equality, restrictions and suspension. Four outputs: requirements matrix, recalculation/correction record, handoff including two communication drafts, and tool reflection.

subject.name: Fundraisers
subject.summary: Occupational definition | O*NET-SOC13-1131.00 Fundraisers organize activities to raise funds, monetary donations or other gifts for organizations, and may design promotional materials explaining the organization's work, goals and funding needs. The 28 tasks include donor relationships/pledges, cash/in-kind sponsorships, databases/acknowledgments, strategies/plans, grant applications, donor/investor research, staff/volunteer supervision, targets/progress, recruitment/outreach, community promotion, reports/presentations, explaining donation tax benefits, publicity/speeches/press releases, budget/cost monitoring, special/online campaigns, speaker invitations, corporate matching, logistics, media contacts and event materials. Management, strategy, events and tax explanations are official tasks and cannot be excluded categorically. Verify personal authority and jurisdictional procedures separately.
